issues.description: The template header declares the image class as 'Image24' while the implementation and the solution use the name 'Bitmap24'. This mismatch (header: Image24 vs. implementation/solution: Bitmap24) breaks the conceptual mapping for the single image/bitmap entity: students reading the header will expect to use Image24, but all example code (main, Bitmap24.cpp) constructs and uses Bitmap24. This will cause compilation failure and unnecessary debugging time as students try to reconcile two different identifiers for the same entity.
issues.suggested_fix: In the template header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) rename the class declaration from 'class Image24' to 'class Bitmap24' (and ensure include guards and any forward declarations match). This aligns the header with the implementation (Bitmap24.cpp) and the solution, removes the compilation/name-mapping mismatch, and makes the intended entity name consistent for students.
